title: Pogačar eyes world championships after successful collarbone surgery
description: Tadej Pogačar underwent successful surgery on his broken left collarbone after his heavy crash at the Vuelta a España, his team doctor Adrian Rotunno said on Monday. The operation went well, Rotunno said, adding that the Slovenian star would remain in hospital for a few days for postoperative monitoring.
fullText:
Tadej Pogačar underwent successful surgery on his broken left collarbone after his heavy crash at the Vuelta a España, his team doctor Adrian Rotunno said on Monday.

The operation went well, Rotunno said, adding that the Slovenian star would remain in hospital for a few days for postoperative monitoring.

Pogačar would travel home as soon as he was able to, where he would begin his recovery and rehabilitation under the supervision of the medical team, Rotunno said.

The injury leaves Pogačar facing a race against time to compete at the road world championships in late September. Team manager Mauro Gianetti had said before the operation that Pogačar could still target the world championships, but that a firm assessment would depend on the surgery.

"Of course it wouldn't be easy to recover for the world championships," Gianetti said on the Vuelta rest day Monday.

Pogačar, who has won the world title for the past two years, suffered a heavy crash during Saturday's eighth stage of the Vuelta. He suffered a collarbone and cervical fracture as well as a concussion.

A broken bone typically takes about six weeks to heal, although cyclists have returned to competition after four weeks in some cases.

Gianetti said he had been deeply concerned immediately after the crash.

"I was a bit relieved when he stood. I said to myself: 'OK, he is standing, walking, he wants to continue.' But of course, that was not possible."

Pogačar had been hoping to win the Vuelta for the first time this year. The five-time Tour de France winner had previously ridden the Spanish Grand Tour only once, finishing third in 2019 at the age of 20.

He also hopes to compete at the world championships in Montreal, with the road race scheduled for September 27, and at the Tour of Lombardy on October 10. Pogačar has won the Italian one-day race, known as the "Race of the Falling Leaves," four years in a row.

title: Detroit Lions Sign OL Elijah Klein
description: The Detroit Lions are signing former Buccaneers offensive lineman Elijah Klein to their practice squad, adding an experienced blocker with versatility across the line.
fullText:
The Detroit Lions are adding some outside experience to their practice squad.

Detroit is signing offensive lineman Elijah Klein, according to Greg Auman. Klein spent the first two seasons of his NFL career with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before being released during final roster cuts Sunday.

The move gives the Lions another developmental lineman with something Detroit clearly values: positional flexibility.

The Buccaneers selected Klein out of UTEP with the 220th overall pick in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft. Tampa Bay viewed his ability to move around the offensive line as one of his strengths from the beginning, noting that Klein primarily played guard in college but also had experience at tackle. Tampa Bay's original Klein draft profile

That versatility continued in the NFL.

Justin Rogers of Detroit Football Network noted that the 6-foot-4, nearly 320-pound Klein has taken preseason snaps at right guard, left guard, center and right tackle over the past two years.

Klein has already appeared in 26 regular-season games with one start, which came at left guard against the New York Jets in 2025. Klein's Buccaneers career page

For a practice-squad addition, that is a decent amount of NFL experience.

Detroit has already brought Mason Miller back after he impressed while handling emergency center duties during the preseason finale. The Lions now add Klein to a practice-squad offensive line that gives them several options if injuries hit the active roster.

That need became more obvious after Cade Mays landed on injured reserve, while Detroit also spent the final weeks of camp sorting through its depth behind a relatively young starting offensive line.

Miller's return gave the Lions one familiar option, and Detroit Sports Nation recently detailed how his unexpected work at center helped earn him another opportunity in the organization. Mason Miller's return to the Lions practice squad

The Lions have also been steadily rebuilding the depth they lost during final roster cuts, with several familiar players returning as Detroit assembled its practice squad Monday. Detroit's first wave of practice-squad additions

Detroit's offensive-line depth was tested during its 25-16 preseason victory over the Indianapolis Colts, and Klein gives the Lions another player capable of covering multiple spots if they need help during the regular season.

He may be starting on the practice squad, but a lineman who can handle four positions and already has 26 NFL games on his résumé is useful insurance to have around.

title: Twins trounce Tigers with homers aplenty
description: The walks sure didn’t help, either.
fullText:
The Tigers went to Minnesota to open a three-game series with their playoff hopes hanging by a thread. They did nothing to assuage their fans' fears on Monday night, dropping said series opener by a 11-1 score.

Starting for the Tigers was Jackson Jobe, making his fifth start this year after recovering from Tommy John surgery. He's struggled with walks: his past two starts have seen him walk three batters in sub-five-inning outings, throwing 86 pitches in each. His stuff has looked good so far, though.

Taj Bradley started for the Twins, and he's been a solid part of their rotation this year; he started his career with a few years in Tampa, and they traded him to Minnesota midway through the 2025 season. His walk rate has really crept up this year to something you shouldn't see in a starter: it was 3.8 per 9 innings coming into today. That wasn't a problem tonight, though.

Minnesota got on the board in the bottom of the first: a leadoff double by Luke Keaschall was followed by a productive groundout and a sacrifice fly by Old Friend™ Kody Clemens. Did you know Clemens had over 20 home runs this year? I sure didn't.

The Twins and Tigers traded nice 5-6-3 double plays in consecutive innings. You don't see that too often.

Clemens wasn't done, though: he mashed a high curveball into the right-field seats for his twenty-third home run of the year to lead off the bottom of the fourth, and the Twins were ahead 2-0. Kevin McGonigle had a rough inning in the field, too: a ground ball slipped under his glove, and on a throw in from the outfield which would've nabbed a runner at second base, he just straight-up dropped it. But a routine fly ball to left field got the Tigers out of the inning without further damage.

Keaschall led off the fifth by reaching base on an error by Hao-Yu Lee at third base, and he stole second. He drew a pickoff attempt by Jobe (heh) which plunked him, so let's just say that the defence wasn't great overall. Clemens walked at the end of a twelve-pitch battle, and Ryan Jeffers followed that with a three-run home run to make it a 5-0 game.

The Tigers got on the board against Bradley with a leadoff no-doubter home run by Lee, going 439 feet into the bullpen to make it a 5-1 game.

Gleyber Torres followed with a sharply-struck single and Colt Keith walked, and you had to wonder, hey, are the Tigers getting something going here? Well, McGonigle flew out to the wall in right field, advancing Torres to third, but alas, Dillon Dingler then hit into a double play and the inning was over. The above clip is, truly, the Tigers' only highlight of the game.

Jobe's night was done after five innings, and his final line was 5 IP, 6 H, 5 R (4 ER), 2 BB, 4 K. So, the control was a little better and the stuff looked decent, but those results just weren't there. The Twins came into tonight's game tied for the most runs scored in the American League, so they aren't exactly pushovers.

Yilber Díaz followed, and while he has a lively arm, he apparently has some trouble controlling where that ball might just end up. He walked the leadoff batter, and after nicely fielding a popup, he walked the next two batters to load the bases with one out. Brooks Lee followed and he cleared said bases with a single; he got thrown out trying to stretch it into a double, but as the old saying goes, "That's like closing the barn door after all the horses have run out."

Meanwhile, Bradley hummed right along into the seventh, and put the maraschino cherry on top of the sundae by striking out Lee on his final pitch of the night; if you round up, it was a 100 mph four-seam fastball and moving all over the place. Tip your cap.

Díaz carried on into the eighth and served up a solo home run to lead off the inning, making it a 9-1 game. But then he got three straight flyouts, so, hooray, I guess?

That extra run allowed Zach McKinstry to take the mound, and John Peck made his Major League debut as a defensive replacement at third base amongst a flurry of defensive changes. McKinstry gave up some runs, of course, but at that point pretty much nobody cared.

Final score: Twins a lot, Tigers not enough

As mentioned, Kody Clemens has over twenty home runs. But did you also know he leads the American League with six triples? I sure didn't know that, either.

It's been a while since Spencer Torkelson's last home run. It was in that Baltimore game near the end of July that we shan't discuss further.

On this day in 1886, an earthquake estimated to be about 7.0 on the Richter scale hit Charleston, South Carolina. If you thought to yourself just now, "I don't think South Carolina is on any major fault lines," you're right: but it's close to a minor fault line in the middle of the North American Plate, and those cracks can definitely produce earthquakes.

title: How to follow US Open on the BBC
description: Everything you need to know about the 2026 US Open, including how to follow the tournament across the BBC.
fullText:
The US Open began on Sunday - and there is comprehensive coverage of the final Grand Slam of the year across the BBC.

The world's top players will gather in New York where, in addition to one of the sport's major prizes, record prize money is on line.

From the return of entertainer Carlos Alcaraz in the men's singles to an eagerly anticipated doubles reunion for Serena and Venus Williams, here is all you need to know.

The US Open main draw begins on Sunday, 30 August.

The 15-day hard court tournament concludes with the men's singles final on Sunday, 13 September, with the women's a day before.

The mixed doubles competition, which became a standalone two-day competition in 2025, took place earlier in the week.

Czech pair Jakub Mensik and Karolina Muchova walked away with the title and $1m in prize money.

Muchova & Mensik win US Open mixed doubles title

Alcaraz and Williams thrill in US Open mixed doubles

Spain's Alcaraz defeated Italian rival Jannik Sinner 6-2 3-6 6-1 6-4 to win the US Open men's singles title last year.

The women's singles title was won by Belarusian Aryna Sabalenka, who beat American Amanda Anisimova 6-3 7-6 (7-3).

The men's doubles competition was won by Spain's Marcel Granollers and Argentine Horacio Zeballos, while Canada's Gabriela Dabrowski and New Zealand's Erin Routliffe won the women's event.

Japan's Tokito Oda and Yui Kamiji won the men's and women's wheelchair singles titles respectively, while Dutchman Niels Vink took the men's quad wheelchair title.

The BBC Sport website will bring you live text commentaries, reports, features and analysis across the fortnight.

BBC Radio 5 Live Sport will provide daily commentaries live from the Arthur Ashe Stadium in New York across BBC Sounds.

Tennis correspondent Russell Fuller will be joined by fellow commentators Katie Smith, Abigail Johnson and David Law, plus summarisers Annabel Croft, Pat Cash, Daniela Hantuchova, Mark Woodforde and Leon Smith.

There will also be podcasts recapping the biggest stories from of the tournament - just search 'tennis' on BBC Sounds to find it.

Two of Britain's big hopes in the singles competitions - Emma Raducanu and Jack Draper - have announced they will not compete at the US Open.

Former US Open winner Raducanu is continuing her recovery from a stress fracture.

The 23-year-old sustained the injury during the grass-court season and was forced to make a late decision to pull out of Wimbledon.

Meanwhile, Draper, a semi-finalist in 2024, has withdrawn because of the long-term arm injury that has stalled his progress.

The 24-year-old former British number one was ranked inside the world's top five when he suffered bone bruising in his left serving arm and has played just 16 matches in the past 12 months.

British qualifier Toby Samuel registered his first win at a Grand Slam with a commanding victory over Tomas Machac on the opening day's play.

Jacob Fearnley, who reached the main draw as a lucky loser, produced a battling five-set victory to reach the second round.

However, British number one Cameron Norrie lost in four sets to Luca Van Assche.

British number one Katie Boulter also reached the first round with a battling 6-4 3-6 6-0 win over American wildcard Carol Young Suh Lee.

Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery, Jan Choinski, and qualifier Harry Wendelken all play later in the week.

Harriet Dart and Francesca Jones also won all three of their qualifying matches, marking the first time four British players have progressed to the main draws of an overseas Grand Slam since the 1988 Australian Open.

Dart reached the second round with a comeback win over American Peyton Stearns.

Samuel breaks more new ground with first win at a Slam

The wait for the return of the exciting rivalry between Alcaraz and Sinner goes on.

Sinner and Alcaraz produced a clean sweep of the Grand Slam titles in both 2024 and 2025, winning four majors apiece in a duopoly which has morphed into a generational duel.

But the pair have not played at the same Grand Slam since January's Australian Open.

Alcaraz was forced to miss the French Open and Wimbledon because of a wrist problem, while a knee issue has ruled Sinner out of the US Open.

Sinner has not competed since he lifted his fifth career Grand Slam singles title by beating Alexander Zverev at the All England Club in July.

Alcaraz, meanwhile, made his return to competitive action alongside American great Serena in the mixed doubles competition in New York on Tuesday, reaching the quarter-finals.

Novak Djokovic was bidding for a standalone record 25th Grand Slam title but suffered a gruelling first-round exit to Mariano Navone.

'I felt the love' - how did Alcaraz look on winning singles return?

Djokovic's tearful loss leaves future uncertain

In the women's event, world number one Sabalenka is aiming to become the first woman since Serena Williams in 2014 to win the title three years in a row.

However, Sabalenka is in shaky form, with her top ranking also under threat.

Elena Rybakina - who beat Sabalenka to win the Australian Open in January - will become number one if she reaches the semi-finals regardless of other results.

Rybakina can become number one without playing a match provided Sabalenka, Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff do not win the title.

One of the big occasions at this year's tournament will be the return of the Williams sisters in a Grand Slam doubles competition.

Serena and Venus have been given a wildcard for the women's doubles, and 46-year-old Venus will also play singles in New York.

Williams sisters given US Open doubles wildcard

The draws for the men's and women's singles competitions at the US Open took place on Thursday, 27 August.

Alcaraz faces Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first round while Sabalenka will play Colombia's Camila Osorio.

The US Open is this year offering the biggest prize fund in Grand Slam history with a total of $108m (£79.2m) up for grabs - marking a 20% increase on last year.

The singles' champions will receive $5.5m (£4.03m) each in a 10% increase on 2025.

First-round losers will take home $140,000 (£102,667) - which is $30,000 and 27% more than last year.

The prize pool includes a $2m (£1.47m) contribution to a welfare fund, which leading players have been demanding from all the Grand Slams.

US Open offers biggest prize fund in Grand Slam history

The mixed doubles took place from 24-26 August.

Muchova and Mensik paired up for the first time to win the mixed doubles title, beating Flavio Cobolli and Belinda Bencic in the final.

The tournament's revamped mixed doubles format has attracted criticism for favouring the allure of the sport's top singles stars at the expense of established doubles players.

But the crowds turned out and produced a terrific atmosphere for the tournament's headline act, Alcaraz and Williams, with about 15,000 people watching inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.

title: Tigers crushed again in loss as Twins put on power show
description: Detroit Tigers score: Jackson Jobe allowed five runs (four earned) in five innings as his teammates struggled against Taj Bradley on Monday.
fullText:
MINNEAPOLIS – It was like watching water circle the drain.

Everything in a spiral. Flowing toward a narrow opening. Gravity tugging it all down. The result all but inevitable.

The Detroit Tigers played sloppy defense against the Minnesota Twins on Monday, Aug. 31. They didn't generate much offense. Jackson Jobe gave up four earned runs, including a pair of homers, en route to five overall. The bullpen gave up four more until Zach McKinstry was brought in to end the misery, though he gave up two more. And the result was all but inevitable – gurgle, gurgle, gurgle – as the Minnesota Twins spanked the Tigers, 11-1, at Target Field.

Which is the fitting theme for what the Tigers have experienced over more than two weeks.

The Tigers (63-74) have now lost 13 of 16 games, dating to August 14.

What has been the big problem? The offense has disappeared.

Consider this: The Tigers began August with a fine 8-3 record and had a plus-40 run differential in just that month.

But in their past 16 games? They have won just three times while being outscored by 35 runs.

Monday's loss dropped the Tigers to six games back in the American League wild-card chase, with the Cleveland Guardians idle, and 9½ back in the AL Central with 25 games to play.

The Tigers are in a weird position. They are still talking about fighting to make the playoffs, even if the odds are against them (and get decidedly worse every day). But they are also in the midst of a youth movement, stacking the roster with rookies. On Monday, they brought up shortstop John Peck, a 2023 draft pick who made his MLB debut in the eighth inning and is expected to start on Tuesday.

"We've watched young players come up and contribute, and so the message doesn't really change – the expectation doesn't change," Tigers manager A.J. Hinch said before the game. "We are where we are, and we know we have to be really, really good to make this a memorable September."

Well, the final day of August was anything but memorable.

Because they couldn't get anything going against Twins starter Taj Bradley, who was simply brilliant. He threw seven dominant innings, allowing just one run while recording nine strikeouts.

Bradley was coming off an 11-strikeout performance against the Athletics on Aug. 25, including the first immaculate inning in Twins history. He wasn't immaculate against the Tigers, but he was a dominant force.

Bradley allowed only one hit through the first four innings – a Hao-Yu Lee single to right. Then again, this looked awfully familiar. Bradley dominated the Tigers on April 7 in a 6⅓-inning performance, allowing just one run and striking out 10.

The one bright spot for the Tigers?

Lee crushed a homer to center that had an exit velocity of 109.6 mph and traveled 439 feet.

The Twins came into this game with a certain style.

"This is a team across the way that's pretty aggressive," Hinch said before the game. "You rarely get to four-pitch at-bats. These guys want to swing the bat."

And that's what they did against Jobe.

Luke Keaschall doubled on Jobe's second pitch Monday. After he moved to third on a fielder's choice, former Tiger Kody Clemens hit a sacrifice fly to give the Twins a 1-0 lead.

Clemens caused more damage in the fourth inning when he crushed a hanging curve that was actually out of the strike zone.

Jobe was in deep trouble in the fourth after a walk, hit and error. But he got out of it with a pair of harmless popups.

Keaschall was a pain in the fifth inning as well. After he got on by a Lee error, Keaschall stole second base – off Jobe. Keaschall seemed to mess with Jobe, taking a massive lead off second; it seemed to mess up the young righty as Jobe walked Clemens to create another tenuous moment. Then Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers hit a three-run homer, his 11th of the season.

Troy Melton (7-3, 1.86) will take the mound for the Tigers when they face the Twins in the second game of this three-game series on Tuesday (7:40 p.m., Detroit SportsNet). Lefty Connor Prielipp (3-7, 5.55) will start for Minnesota.

title: Michigan State offensive lineman nominated for 2026 Campbell Trophy
description: A Michigan State offensive lineman was nominated for the 2026 Campbell Trophy.
fullText:
Michigan State football brought in North Dakota State center transfer Trent Fraley in to patrol the middle of their offensive line in 2026. Not only will Fraley be a big help on the field, but by all accounts, Fraley is a top leader and a great person to have off of the field.

Fraley's off field presence was made known even more when he was named as Michigan State's nominee for the Campbell Trophy. Awarded by the National Football Federation, the Campbell Trophy is given to a player with the best combination of academics, leadership and on-field performance. It has been dubbed as the "Academic Heisman."

title: Why AEW’s announcers made the right call for stunning All In finish
description: All Elite Wrestling, better known as AEW, put on its biggest show of the year at Wembley Stadium on Sunday. The main event featured champion Kenny Omega, arguably the greatest wrestler of his generation, up against the United Kingdom’s favorite wrestling son, the “Aerial Assassin” Will Ospreay. This was as good of a matchup on…
fullText:
All Elite Wrestling, better known as AEW, put on its biggest show of the year at Wembley Stadium on Sunday.

The main event featured champion Kenny Omega, arguably the greatest wrestler of his generation, up against the United Kingdom's favorite wrestling son, the "Aerial Assassin" Will Ospreay.

This was as good of a matchup on paper as you can set up in the world of professional wrestling, and from the phenomenally produced entrances to the action in the ring to the thrilling finish, it lived up to the billing. Ospreay won the title on home soil, sending the crowd home happy and positioning him as one of the top faces of AEW for years to come.

While there's plenty to talk about regarding the match, one moment stands out above the rest, and it wound up serving as a litmus test for fans' preferences on how announcers handle the biggest moments in sports.

The most stunning moment of the match came after Omega hit his finishing move, the One-Winged Angel, on Ospreay in the middle of the ring. As the crowd and referee counted in unison, "One, two," Omega threw a fist in the air in presumed victory. But Ospreay kicked out.

The pop from the crowd was absolutely outrageous. Watch below.

.@WILLOSPREAY KICKED OUT OF THE ONE WINGED ANGEL!

Watch #AEWAllIn London LIVE on HBO Max PPV pic.twitter.com/PNJKluWbvA

— All Elite Wrestling (@AEW) August 30, 2026

You might be wondering just why the moment got such a loud reaction. Sure, this was the main event of the night and a title fight, but kicking out at two in hardly uncommon in professional wrestling — it is in fact the most tried and true method of building tension as a match edges towards a conclusion.

But Ospreay's kick out was different, because the One-Winged Angel is different.

Omega's One-Winged Angel is probably the most well protected finisher in all of wrestling — when it lands, it lands, and it ends with Omega winning on a three count. While a few notable wrestlers have been able to scramble their way out of defeat after taking a One-Winged Angel from Omega by touching the ropes or some referee shenanigans, just one man has kicked out of the finisher clean — Omega's longtime tag-team partner Kota Ibushi, who did it in 2012.

You may be thinking that such context is silly to consider, as the endings of professional wrestling matches are planned out in advance, and thus such a memorable moment can be manipulated into existence. This fails to appreciate the art that goes into making such a decision. This is a moment that was literally 14 years in the making, and it's a bullet that Omega can only fire once for maximum impact. Giving it to Ospreay in this spot is an incredible gesture.

That context is important, and raises the question — why wasn't it brought up in the broadcast? Instant reactions to the moment online showed that some fans were disappointed that a bigger deal wasn't made out of the fact that in the reality of professional wrestling, the near-impossible had just happened.

Why was commentary legit dead? Like someone kicked out of the legendary one winged angel… give me something to show how big a deal it is! pic.twitter.com/xjw8H5alOU

— Sonal (@Wrestling_Chat) August 30, 2026

But plenty of others loved how the broadcast handled the moment. The stunned silence and letting the moment breathe, allowing the audience reaction to tell the story, resembled what you might see on a more traditional sports broadcast.

an american promotion’s commentary team actually let a massive moment breathe while letting the crowd response do the talking for them and people are responding with “why didn’t we get excalibur going OH WOW… WOW… I canNOT believe it!!” https://t.co/mWXjYineDq

— chris (@fighthaskins) August 31, 2026

There are merits to both sides of the argument. Watching the longer cut of the moment that AEW posted to YouTube, you might wonder why the commentary team didn't mention more about just how shocking it was to see Will Ospreay to kick out once they had given the audience the microphone for a bit.

It's also worth noting that heading into the match, it was widely expected that Ospreay would win, and many fans anticipated that he would kick out of the One-Winged Angel as a part of the match. In the context of the moment, it was simultaneously shocking to all and expected by some. This does not take away from the moment, but it does add another wrinkle to the question of how to call the action.

Ultimately, letting it breathe feels like it was the right move. In another reality, Excalibur or another member of the commentary team jumped in and screamed, "OH MY GOD! HE'S DONE IT! HE KICKED OUT OF THE ONE-WINGED ANGEL!!" and the sides of the debate are flipped — in fact chances are that more people would be mad about stepping on the moment than those currently frustrated with the silence.

cant enjoy anything if excalibur and tony arent screaming “WHAT AN ALL IN MOMENT” in my ear https://t.co/B86GjgJZif

— Ren (@RenZarathustra1) August 31, 2026

Regardless of where you land on the debate, the moment is an interesting litmus test regarding what you, the audience member, values out of commentary.

One of my favorite moments in modern broadcasting is Joe Buck's call of the Minneapolis Miracle.

"Diggs! Sideline! Touchdown! Unbelievable! Vikings win it!"

After that succinct summary, he lays out and lets the cheers of the crowd tell the story.

There is a balance to these things, and when the crowd reaction is fantastic, it's probably best to air on the side of letting that reaction explain the gravity of what just happened. Commentators can always add context to the moment while analyzing the replay, but the moment itself only can happen once, and in the moment, the crowd is more important that anything a commentator can say.

On Sunday, the moment was literally 14 years in the making, and a culminating act of two of the greatest performers of their generation. The AEW audience is not as casual as the WWE audience, and the wide majority of fans tuning in likely knew the full significance of the scene that was playing out and the buildup of Ospreay and Omega's careers to that particular moment in time.

The pop they got from the crowd was earned, and the fact that we have that reaction clean on tape forever is a good thing. Commentators can talk over the replay now as much as they want, but the moment belonged to Omega, Ospreay, and the Wembley crowd.

title: GB's Fearnley and Dart complete superb comeback wins
description: Britons Jacob Fearnley and Harriet Dart both produce remarkable comeback wins to reach the US Open second round.
fullText:
Britain's Jacob Fearnley produced a remarkable comeback to beat Martin Landaluce in five sets after compatriot Harriet Dart ended a 19-month wait for a Grand Slam win in the US Open first round.

World number 101 Fearnley, playing in the main draw as a lucky loser, trailed 5-2 in the fourth set before reeling off 10 of the next 11 games en route to a thrilling 4-6 6-2 4-6 7-5 6-3 win.

Dart, taken to three sets in all three of her US Open qualifying matches – including losing the opening set against Kristina Penickova and Heather Watson – once again opted for the scenic route at Flushing Meadows.

Down a set and a break, she took advantage of the fluctuating form of American opponent Peyton Stearns to win 3-6 6-3 6-2.

Fearnley and Dart join fellow Brits Toby Samuel and Katie Boulter in round two, where they will face 27th seed Tomas Etcheverry and 25th seed Marie Bouzkova, respectively.

After giving up a one-set lead against Jurij Rodionov in his final qualifying match, Fearnley was handed a "second chance" following the late withdrawal of Brazilian Joao Fonseca.

Knowing he didn't have a "whole lot to lose" and taking inspiration from a comeback win on the Challenger Tour in July, the British number four added another great escape to his season by following a simple philosophy – "just point after point".

Seemingly down and out with world number 65 Landaluce serving for the match in the fourth set, Fearnley won 20 of the next 24 points, including three breaks of serve, to force an unlikely decider.

Continuing that momentum, he roared into a 5-1 lead in the fifth. Although he failed to serve out the win at the first attempt, letting two match points go by, double-faulting at two crucial moments and completely missing a smash, he recovered his composure to serve out to love in his next service game.

Across the dramatic final two sets, Fearnley (27) and Landaluce (29) were evenly matched for unforced errors, but the Briton struck an impressive 30 winners to his opponent's 11 as he seized the initiative.

"I still don't think I've comprehended it but a couple of weeks ago, I was playing in the final in Newport and I was 5-1, 40-15 down," Fearnley said.

"I ended up winning, so it felt like this one was possible.

"The way I was seeing it was that I don't have a lot to lose."

Dart arrived in New York having not won a main-draw singles match at a major since reaching the second round of the 2025 Australian Open.

She failed to qualify for four of the next six Grand Slams and fell at the first hurdle at the past two editions of Wimbledon after receiving a wildcard on each occasion.

However, cheered on by her parents, uncle, and numerous cousins at her "home away from home", Dart downed Stearns to reach the US Open second round for the third time.

The 30-year-old immediately ran to celebrate with her team, which now includes 2013 Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli.

The pair linked up in January and this latest win builds on a run to the quarter-finals at July's Challenger tournament in Vancouver and qualification for the Cincinnati Open in August.

"From her experience, she knows what I'm going through, how I'm feeling, how the day starts, how it finishes - everything from the little things to the big things," Dart said of Bartoli.

"To be able to soak up everything, all of her experience, and learn from her - I feel I'm learning so much every time we speak.

"I feel like I'm improving at a lot of things, which motivates me."

Dart could not convert any of her four break points in the opening game of the match, with Stearns not offering up another opportunity in the first set.

Stearns piled relentless pressure on the Briton's serve, eventually breaking in the eighth game.

Dart was broken for a second time in the opening game of the second set but, aided by an increasingly erratic Stearns, whose 40 winners were offset by 47 unforced errors, she secured two breaks of her own to force a decider.

Taking control midway through the third set, Dart completed a crucial hold in the sixth game to end a run of three consecutive breaks before converting her fourth match point to seal a nervy win in a little under two and a half hours.

title: 'I felt the love' - how did Alcaraz look on winning singles return?
description: After a 139-day wait, Carlos Alcaraz makes a winning return to the singles court as he beats Roman Safuillin in the US Open first round.
fullText:
After a 139-day wait, Carlos Alcaraz is back to winning ways on the singles court.

The seven-time major winner walked on to Arthur Ashe Stadium on Monday to begin his US Open title defence after spending just over four months on the sidelines with a wrist injury.

And he delighted fans with his entertaining brand of tennis and infectious energy as he beat Russia's Roman Safiullin 6-4 6-4 6-4.

Alcaraz was forced to watch from the sidelines as rivals Alexander Zverev and Jannik Sinner lifted the French Open and Wimbledon titles this summer.

However, the Spaniard is finally back - and grateful to be competing again.

"I missed the crowd, the energy, the competition – I missed everything," a smiling Alcaraz said in his on-court interview.

"I'm just really, really happy that I was able to compete again."

Despite playing with a compression sleeve on his right arm, Alcaraz unleashed his trademark forehand with familiar ferocity. The whippy stroke accounted for the majority of his 28 winners against Safiullin.

"I felt great. I don't know how it looked from outside, but from inside, my feeling was that I was hitting normal," Alcaraz said.

"I was playing pretty normal, playing my style, and everything felt great."

Each of Alcaraz's winners was met with a clenched fist and celebratory cry of "vamos" - Spanish for "let's go" - towards his team on the side of the court.

The 23-year-old clearly enjoyed the occasion, smiling after points and, at one stage, singing along to a Michael Jackson song at the change of ends.

When he ended an intense rally with a sublime drop shot during his final service game, Alcaraz lifted his fist to the sky before pointing to his ear and waving his arms to demand more noise from the raucous crowd.

Former Wimbledon champion Pat Cash said on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra that it looked as though "every little win" was celebrated by Alcaraz.

"What I really want to do is enjoy every time that I'm going to walk into the court, feeling the energy from the people," Alcaraz said.

"That's what I'm going do this tournament. The results, it's going to come after all.

"That's why I enjoyed so much today, and it wasn't a surprise for me, because I came here to enjoy."

Even though Alcaraz enjoyed his first-round match at Flushing Meadows, there are improvements to be made as he continues his comeback.

While he impressed with his forehand and delicate drop shots, his serve did not carry the threat it usually does.

The defending champion managed just two aces to five double faults - although he did land 68% of his first serves and won 66% of the points behind it.

"The serve is the shot I was struggling [with] the most," Alcaraz explained, although he added that a slower serve was an intentional tactic to catch Safiullin out.

"I'm going try to serve better. The point is going to try to serve normal, but it's a shot that I just always struggle [with].

"But it will be back, for sure."

Alcaraz did not look overly short of match fitness, but he admitted he had doubts before his encounter with Safiullin over his ability to compete over five sets.

"There were some doubts in the match, I'm not going to lie," he said.

"I've been thinking about 'am I going to last the best of five, am I going to last playing four sets, five sets?'.

"I need more matches under the belt to get again into the rhythm of the tournament. I'm pretty sure I'm going to get better and better every day."

There will be tougher tests than world number 99 Safiullin for Alcaraz, who will face Portugal's 72nd-ranked Jaime Faria next.

However, his path to the final does seem to have opened up considerably.

World number one Sinner is absent because of a knee problem, while 24-time Grand Slam champion Novak Djokovic suffered a shock first-round exit to Argentina's Mariano Navone on Sunday.

As the second seed, Alcaraz is on the opposite side of the draw to French Open champion and top seed Zverev, and the pair cannot meet until the final.

Meanwhile, French 10th seed Arthur Fils - viewed by many as a title contender after winning the Cincinnati Masters earlier this month - went out earlier on Monday as he lost to Stefanos Tsitsipas of Greece.

It means that the only top-10 player that Alcaraz can meet before the semi-finals is American Ben Shelton.

Shelton, who is one of several home players aiming to end their nation's 23-year wait for a men's champion, made a nervous start in his opening match before fighting back for a 1-6 6-1 7-6 (7-3) 6-2 win against Dutch opponent Tallon Griekspoor.

title: Sabalenka wins to begin bid for US Open 'three-peat'
description: Aryna Sabalenka blocks out the noise to overcome a tricky first-round test against Camila Osorio and begin her bid for a historic US Open "three-peat".
fullText:
Aryna Sabalenka blocked out the noise to overcome a tricky first-round test against Camila Osorio and begin her bid for a historic US Open "three-peat".

The two-time defending champion has suffered a dip in form in recent months after a stellar start to the season in which she reached the Australian Open final and completed the 'Sunshine Double' at Indian Wells and Miami.

Sabalenka's position as world number one is now under serious threat and she risks ending the year without a Grand Slam title for the first time since 2022.

However, she avoided an early slip-up as she held off a resilient Osorio to win 6-2 6-4 on her return to Arthur Ashe Stadium.

"I really feel my best emotions at this stadium so it means a lot to be back and have an opportunity for a 'three-peat'," Sabalenka said.

"I'm trying to focus on myself. I'm enjoying my time in New York and I'm ready to go out here and do anything it takes to get the wins.

When Sabalenka lifted the Miami Open trophy in April, she established a 3,000-point lead at the top of the world rankings.

But early exits - by her high standards at least - followed at the French Open and Wimbledon. Now, Australian Open champion Elena Rybakina, who faces American wildcard Thea Frodin on Tuesday, trails her by just 434 points.

It means that Sabalenka, who is defending 2,000 points at Flushing Meadows, will have to win the title and hope Rybakina falls before the semi-finals to extend her 99-week reign as world number one.

Home favourites Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff could also secure the number one ranking with a title triumph.

Should Sabalenka win a third successive US Open title, she would become only the third woman to do so in the Open era after Serena Williams and Chris Evert.

However, she will need to improve considerably to navigate a stacked draw in New York.

Sabalenka stormed through the first set against the 52nd-ranked Osorio but struggled in the second, landing 48% of her first serves and hitting 12 unforced errors.

But the four-time major singles champion fended off three break points and struck decisively at 4-4 before serving out victory after one hour and 28 minutes.

Sabalenka will face Russian qualifier Polina Iatcenko next.

Later on Monday, American Amanda Anisimova celebrated her 25th birthday with a dominant 6-1 6-3 win against compatriot Ashlyn Krueger.

The crowd on Louis Armstrong treated the 10th seed, who was runner-up to Sabalenka at last year's US Open, with a rendition of 'happy birthday' afterwards.

Six-time major champion Iga Swiatek, who won the title in 2022 but is seeded eighth after a below-par season, made a solid start with a 6-2 6-3 victory over China's Wang Xiyu.

Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova made it safely through with a 7-5 6-1 win over American Katie Volynets, while Karolina Muchova, who lost to Noskova in the SW19 final, dropped just three games in a 58-minute demolition of Austria's Sinja Kraus.

French Open finalist Maja Chwalinska was less fortunate as she fell to a 6 2 6-3 defeat by home hope Taylor Townsend.

title: Republicans ask Supreme Court to let them air TV ads for less
description: Republican campaign groups – supported by the Trump administration – asked the Supreme Court on Monday to let them purchase television advertising at discounted rates
fullText:
Republican campaign groups – supported by the Trump administration – asked the Supreme Court on Monday to let them purchase television advertising at discounted rates, handing the nation's highest court another emergency appeal that could influence the outcome of this year's midterm elections.

The quick-turn appeal follows a series of high-profile decisions from the 6-3 conservative court that have largely benefited Republicans. A separate case dealing with President Donald Trump's controversial executive order on mail ballots is also expected to rocket back to the justices in the coming days.

The latest case involves television advertising, often the most expensive part of a congressional campaign. Candidates benefit from a federal law that requires broadcasters to charge them deeply discounted ad rates. Earlier this year, the Federal Communications Commission said that political parties and other entities are also entitled to the lower rates.

The FCC decision was widely seen as benefiting the Republican Party, which generally tends to raise more money through the party committees. Democrats, by contrast, generally raise more money directly through their candidates.

The House and Senate Republican party committees told the Supreme Court on Monday that they had "budgeted tens of millions of dollars in ad buys under these rules." But, because of the appeals court decision, "broadcast stations are already rescinding those rates."

The Republican committees argued in their filing that federal courts lack jurisdiction to decide the case because the FCC's "interpretive guidance" was "neither agency action, nor final."

They have asked the court to act by Friday.

The Trump administration, which is eager to keep Republican control of Congress, submitted a brief shortly after the appeal was filed supporting the GOP groups. The Justice Department argued that the FCC guidance doesn't harm the Democratic candidates who sued because the rule is applied universally to all candidates and groups.

"The notice does not grant favored treatment to one side or the other; instead, the notice's interpretation offers the same benefit to all sides, including the challengers themselves and the committees and parties supporting them," Solicitor General D. John Sauer, the administration's top appellate attorney, told the Supreme Court.

A divided three-judge panel of the 4th US Circuit Court of Appeals ruled last week that federal law provides the lower rate only for candidates.

"The term 'candidate' means 'candidate,'" wrote US Circuit Judge Robert King, who was appointed to the bench by President Bill Clinton.

US Circuit Judge J. Harvie Wilkinson III, a long-serving conservative appointed by President Ronald Reagan, dissented. He argued that collaboration between candidates and parties has a rich tradition in the United States and described the 4th Circuit's decision as an "assault" on that tradition.

"Congress cannot dangle lower rates for some candidate speech as a means of penalizing other candidate speech," he wrote.

Four Democratic candidates sued over the FCC's decision: Rep. Kristen McDonald Rivet of Michigan, former Sen. Sherrod Brown of Ohio, Sen. Jon Ossoff of Georgia, and former Gov. Roy Cooper of North Carolina. The campaign arm for House and Senate Republicans intervened to defend the FCC's decision.

The Supreme Court in late June rolled back longstanding limits on how much political parties may coordinate with federal candidates. Since the 1970s, political party committees were capped at how much money they may spend in coordination with a campaign. That pushed a flood of campaign money toward super PACs, which have no spending limits, but are unable to run their advertising and other messages past candidates they want to help.

In a 6-3 decision decided along ideological lines, the court ruled that those caps violated the First Amendment. That decision was a victory for Republicans principally because of the ad rate issue.

The Supreme Court is likely to act on the emergency appeal in coming weeks.

title: Arteta joins elite 250 club - but where does he rank?
description: At full-time in Arsenal's 1-0 win at Aston Villa, the travelling supporters sang about how their team will win the league again with Mikel Arteta in charge.
fullText:
When thinking of the greatest managers of the Premier League era, Arsene Wenger, Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola are names that belong high on the list.

They are three of the rare breed to have managed 250 games with a single Premier League club, and Mikel Arteta is now the 10th member of that elite group.

Monday's 1-0 win over Aston Villa was the 250th top-flight game in charge for Arteta with the Gunners, and his champions delivered a trademark performance.

At full-time at Villa Park, the travelling supporters sang about how they are going to win the league again with Arteta in charge.

With Arsenal coming into this season as trophy holders, and with transition affecting rivals Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea and Manchester United, it is hard to see how the fans' partisan prediction is going to be proved wrong.

Arsenal conceded the fewest goals in the league last season as they won the title for the first time in 22 years.

And during Arteta's nearly seven years in charge, the Gunners have become renowned for their defensive excellence.

Against Aston Villa they showed it again, without allowing a shot on target against them as Bukayo Saka's second-half goal secured victory.

The latest win not only puts Arteta in the 250 club. He also has the fourth-best win percentage among those bosses, with only Guardiola, Ferguson and Jurgen Klopp ahead of him.

Arteta is the longest-serving current Premier League manager and with his longevity has come an Arsenal identity.

Arsenal have become renowned for being difficult to break down and new players repeatedly say that they are impressed and sometimes overwhelmed by the level of detail coming from Arteta.

This is the fifth season in a row where Arsenal have won their first two Premier League matches and they again have a solid platform to build another title challenge.

The Gunners have only faced three shots on target in their first two Premier League games. Villa drew a blank in that regard.

During their title triumph last season, the Gunners did not allow their opponents a shot on target in six league matches, the joint-most of any side in a campaign on record since the 2003-04 season.

Goalkeeper David Raya has won the the Golden Glove award for the most clean sheets in each of the past three seasons, while William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhaes have been voted in the PFA team of the year for the past three seasons too.

Since the start of March, the Gunners have kept eight Premier League clean sheets – three more than any other side and the only side in Europe's big-five leagues to have kept more are Juventus with nine.

"It's how they defend as a team and how they attack as a team," Arsenal's record goalscorer Thierry Henry told Sky Sports after the game.

"One thing is sure with Arsenal - everybody needs to run. You don't have any passengers in that team. This is how you win a title. You can see they are so good at it."

Saka scores only goal as Arsenal beat Villa

How did match-winner Saka do? Aston Villa v Arsenal ratings

Arsenal have one of the best squads in Europe.

The Gunners spent £250m last summer bringing in eight players as they won the title and have already spent about £200m this year, turning Piero Hincapie's loan deal into a permanent one (£34.5m), signing Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United (£75m), Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge (£34m) and bringing in Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa (£55m).

"That is what we need," Arteta said, speaking to Sky Sports when asked about his squad depth.

"The players that come in make the difference. All of them contributed to create more dominance and more momentum.

"The level of focus and the way they want to contribute to the team, that is going to be decisive in the season."

Arsenal's strength in depth cannot be understated, but one area they may still look to strengthen in is the forward area.

The Gunners have been on the hunt for an elite forward to lift their attack and still could be active on Tuesday's deadline day.

They had an unsuccessful pursuit of Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr, while they also have a long-standing interest in Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez.

"We are trying to improve the squad and until tomorrow night we will try to do it," Arteta said.

"I have been disconnected from the world for the last 24 hours because my energy has to be on the match, but I will get back on it now."

When pushed about a deal for Alvarez, Arteta said: "I don't know, that's for the people upstairs."

Whatever happens in Arsenal's search, they are going to be hard to keep off the top of the table with Arteta at the helm.

title: China warns of 'consequences' over Taiwan presence at Pacific leaders meeting

fullText:
SYDNEY/WELLINGTON, Sept 1 (Reuters) - China said it had serious concerns about Taiwan's presence at the annual Pacific Islands Forum in Palau, warning of "consequences" after the democratically ruled island ‌attended the group's opening ceremony on Monday.

China views Taiwan as its own territory, and China-Taiwan tensions ‌have featured prominently at the meeting, which is intended to demonstrate regional unity.

"There will always be consequences," Qian Bo, China's special envoy for Pacific ​island affairs, said of Taiwan attending the event. "It's not a threat," he said without specifying what the consequences would be.

"This is objected to by all, so this should not have happened. We think it's very inappropriate to do so," he told reporters on Monday after an opening ceremony in Palau, an archipelago of over 500 islands that has maintained diplomatic ties ‌with Taiwan.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said "the ⁠Pacific Islands Forum determines what happens here, not any other country," when asked by reporters about the Chinese envoy's remarks.

"This is primarily a gathering of the Pacific family ... and I ⁠look forward to the engagement," Albanese said on Tuesday.

New Zealand's Foreign Minister, Winston Peters, echoed this sentiment, saying the group does not take instructions from countries outside of it.

"Taiwan is honoured to serve as a partner in the Pacific, continuing to stand ​with ​everyone and work together to make the Pacific more prosperous ​and peaceful," Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung said on ‌Monday.

Lin Chia-lung was invited for meetings and side events held alongside the forum. Taiwan is not a formal dialogue partner of the forum like China, but a development partner. The U.S., EU, Britain, Canada, India and Japan are also among the 21 dialogue partners of the forum.

China has gradually whittled away the number of Pacific Island countries with formal ties to Taipei, with only three remaining — Palau, Tuvalu and the Marshall Islands.

The leaders of Fiji, Vanuatu, Samoa, Solomon ‌Islands and Kiribati did not attend the gathering of the 18-member ​group that counts Australia, New Zealand and Pacific island nations as ​members. Ministers are attending in their place.

Though China ​is Australia's largest trading partner, Canberra remains wary of Beijing's expanding influence in the Pacific ‌and has stepped up security and development ties with ​island nations to deter any ​permanent Chinese military presence in the region.

Australia, New Zealand and the United States have long considered the South Pacific to fall within their sphere of influence.

In the latest sign of that effort, New Zealand and ​the U.S., in a joint statement released ‌on Tuesday during the summit, said they would jointly fund a major upgrade of a World ​War Two port on a Cook Islands' atoll.

title: Billions in US aid to Ukraine under microscope as corruption rocks Zelenskyy’s inner circle
description: Over 24 federal agencies oversee billions in U.S. defense aid to Ukraine as Zelenskyy dismisses officials amid widening anti-corruption probes, expert says.
fullText:
Washington is relying on extensive safeguards and dozens of oversight agencies to scrutinize and protect billions of dollars in U.S. aid to Ukraine amid the country's continuing struggle with corruption, a regional security expert said Sunday.

The oversight comes as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's inner circle faces renewed political pressure from widening investigations, with several senior officials and aides resigning, being dismissed or facing investigations since 2025.

Zelenskyy dismissed Iryna Mudra, a deputy head of the presidential office, on Aug. 19 as anti-corruption investigators pursued a money-laundering case involving another deputy head of the office.

Investigators have not named Mudra as a suspect, The Associated Press reported.

Zelenskyy Says Putin 'Lost The Initiative' As Ukraine's Tech Industry Reshapes The War

"Of course, in all of the former Soviet Union countries, there is significant corruption," former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Carrie Filipetti, now executive director of the Vandenberg Coalition, told Fox News Digital.

"A lot more work needs to be done. But we know, at least on the U.S. side, as we're providing support for their military, we have a lot of mechanisms," she said before explaining how dozens of agencies are working on oversight of U.S. aid to Ukraine.

The U.S. committed $67.8 billion in defense articles and services to Ukraine from February 2022 through March 2026 through the Presidential Drawdown Authority, the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative and Foreign Military Financing, congressional reports show.

That support is part of a broader U.S. response to the war.

About $195 billion has been appropriated for Operation Atlantic Resolve, including funds to replenish U.S. weapons stocks, support U.S. military operations in Europe and provide economic, development and humanitarian assistance, according to the Council on Foreign Relations.

As Trump's Nato Gamble Pays Off, Envoy Names Allies He's Still Watching

"Over 24 federal agencies are involved in oversight," Filipetti said. "To make certain that there are no consequences to the U.S. taxpayer, to our equipment in terms of the corruption issue, U.S. contributions are very much protected."

In recent months, however, senior Ukrainian officials have resigned, been dismissed or faced scrutiny by the country's independent anti-corruption bodies, including Nabu.

Those developments include Andriy Yermak's Nov. 28, 2025, resignation after investigators searched his premises and Mudra's Aug. 19 dismissal during a money-laundering probe.

Former Deputy Prime Minister Olha Stefanishyna was dismissed by Zelenskyy as Ukraine's ambassador to the U.S. on Aug. 3, two days before a suspicion notice was served against her, according to the Kyiv Post.

He also fired Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov on July 15 in a broader reshuffle over internal wartime disagreements which sparked protests across the nation.

Zelenskyy Pressures Us And Europe For More 'Air Defense' Assistance Amid Ongoing War With Russia

In interviews after he left government, Fedorov also complained about what he described as ingrained corruption and patronage networks, Reuters reported.

"We've seen that Zelenskyy is taking really seriously the criticisms of corruption, and every time there is an allegation, he moves very swiftly to remove those individuals from the government," Filipetti said.

"And the fact that there are these independent bodies is, I think, really important. They're listening to them. They're making sure that they're trying to root it out as much as humanly possible."

The Two Most Important American Weapons Systems Nato Is Eager To Have

Zelenskyy has pushed back on suggestions that the investigations implicate him personally.

"The heads of anti-corruption agencies have zero questions for me," Zelenskyy said in remarks published Aug. 23 regarding the investigations. "They understand perfectly well that I am not involved in anything like that."

A February 2024 USAID inspector general review also found that the agency did not independently verify some Ukrainian health workers' salary claims before reimbursement, though Filipetti said U.S. economic aid is now reimbursed only after verification.

"A lot of what the United States has been providing, we're making sure that everything is through a reimbursement mechanism," Filipetti said.

Top Ukrainian Officials In Zelenskyy Government Submit Resignations Amid $100 Million Corruption Scandal

She said U.S. aid has not been tied to the money-laundering allegations and remains protected as Ukraine works to combat corruption.

The scrutiny also comes as Kyiv faces shortages of Patriot interceptors amid intensified Russian strikes and a need for air defense interceptors.

Zelenskyy said he wants to secure 300 additional interceptors for the coming winter, while Ukraine's air force has requested 360.

"One of the most urgent needs that the Ukrainians have right now is interceptor missiles," Filipetti said. "This is why this idea of sending Patriot capabilities and allowing them to produce them on the ground in Ukraine has become so important to Zelenskyy."

Russia's Gas Gamble Backfires As Trump's Energy Vision Reshapes Europe

President Donald Trump has expressed reluctance to further deplete U.S. missile inventories, saying the United States also needs the weapons, while pressing European allies to shoulder more of Ukraine's defense burden.

"We want missiles too," Trump said Aug. 6 when asked about Zelenskyy's requests for long-range missiles and Patriot systems. "Biden gave him so much, Biden gave $300 billion worth of ammunition."

Filipetti also said Ukraine's anti-corruption efforts remain an important consideration for its NATO aspirations.

"I think every country has been really adamant that the Ukrainians move forward in their anti-corruption mechanisms," Filipetti said.

"Obviously, if Ukraine ever wants to be a formal member of NATO, that's something that they will need to prove and demonstrate."

title: Max Miller and ex-girlfriend Stephanie Grisham ordered to remove social media posts in GOP lawmaker’s latest court fight
description: GOP Rep. Max Miller spent Monday morning not on the campaign trail, but Zooming into an Ohio courtroom in a dispute with ex-girlfriend and former White House press secretary Stephanie Grisham, the sec...
fullText:
GOP Rep. Max Miller spent Monday morning not on the campaign trail, but Zooming into an Ohio courtroom in a dispute with ex-girlfriend and former White House press secretary Stephanie Grisham, the second time the embattled congressman has been forced to appear in county court in less than a week.

As House lawmakers return to Washington for a sprint ahead of the midterms, Miller appeared from DC via Zoom to address whether he violated a 2023 settlement agreement with Grisham. That agreement came after Grisham alleged Miller abused her, he denied the allegation and then sued her for defamation. As part of their deal, Grisham and Miller were barred from disparaging each other publicly.

It's the latest legal battle facing Miller as he runs for re-election in a district Trump won in 2024 by more than 10 points but Republicans now fear will be competitive over his legal and personal issues. The congressman has faced calls from some Senate Republicans to step down, but Speaker Mike Johnson told CNN on Monday that he supports Miller's reelection bid, calling him "a great member of Congress."

Miller is also locked in a bitter custody battle with his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, the daughter of GOP Sen. Bernie Moreno. She has alleged that Miller abused her, including holding a gun to her when their daughter was an infant. Miller has denied the allegations. Miller came to court in person in that custody case last week.

Zooming in to the wood-paneled courtroom Monday, Miller faced questions over his social media habits, recent media interviews and whether he called Grisham a liar after the two of them entered into the 2023 settlement agreement.

After hours of testimony, the judge issued preliminary injunctions against Miller and Grisham and ordered both parties to take down numerous social media posts that could be construed as disparaging the other.

Miller was pressed on a post from his X account on May 7 describing audio of Emily Moreno discussing allegations Grisham made against the congressman. Along with the audio, the post read, "here is a recording from 2024. In it, Ms. Emily Moreno admits 1.) everything alleged by Stephanie Grisham was fabricated."

Grisham told the court the post had caused damage to her reputation and shattered the peace she sought in the aftermath of the 2023 settlement agreement.

"When a sitting member of Congress calls you a liar, that is a pretty big deal in political circles," Grisham testified.

Miller argued he never posted any of the material himself and does not have social media on his cell phone. He also argued that his job makes him too busy to be concerned with constant updates to social media, and blamed the May 7 posts on staffers.

"I didn't instruct them to do this, period. They just did it," Miller said of the posts.  "You are making it seem like Twitter is 90 percent of a congressman's job."

The congressman was also pressed on two separate news interviews he did, including one with CNN's Jake Tapper.

In that interview, Tapper asked Miller specifically about Grisham and Moreno's allegations and whether people were supposed to believe they were lying. Miller told Tapper "yes," which Grisham's lawyers argued was a breach of the agreement.

At another point in the interview, Miller told Tapper that he could not get into details about the Grisham allegations because of a settlement agreement that had been reached.

Miller argued in court Monday that he was merely defending himself in the interviews, and that Grisham disparaged him first in the court of public opinion. He also argued that public accusations can cause reputational harm even if they are not true.

"We live in a society where the court of public opinion matters more than facts, at least in my world," he told the court.

The congressman's lawyer Adam Brown alleged that Grisham posted on April 22 about Miller, although she did not do so by name. Brown pointed to a post in which Grisham wrote on X on April 22, "Today I feel broken over what so many men with money and power get away with over & over & over," with a broken heart emoji. "Almost worse is those of you who know & do/say nothing as it happens time & again."

April 22 was the same day that TMZ published a story about Miller with the headline "police investigate child neglect claims in nasty custody battle."

Grisham testified the post was not about Miller, but was a reference to several developments in the ongoing controversy around convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, which has generated regular news headlines.

During her testimony, Grisham also argued that Miller's statements about her had an impact on her personal and professional life, that she suffered from worsening anxiety and often turned down opportunities to participate in television appearances out of fear that she may be asked about Miller, an issue she said she couldn't address given the settlement agreement.

"It has been horrible," she said.

CNN's Alison Main, Manu Raju and Casey Riddle contributed

title: DSA leader's working-class image takes hit as public records pile up contradictions
description: Gustavo Gordillo, NYC Democratic Socialists of America co-chair, faces scrutiny over claims about his immigrant parents, union status and housing.
fullText:
The contradictions are piling up around New York City Democratic Socialists of America co-chair Gustavo Gordillo, whose claims about his working-class credentials — from being a "union electrician" to his housing and family story — have increasingly collided with public records and other evidence.

Gordillo has repeatedly invoked his family's immigrant success story while explaining his support for socialism.

"My parents came here, they had nothing," Gordillo told the New York Times in a profile piece earlier this month. "Their first jobs were in fast food and cleaning houses. They built success in this country. And they're absolutely the exception."

According to Gordillo, he advances the cause of socialism because he believes it can "build a world" where his parents' success story is "not exceptional."

Luxury Travel, Shopping, Six-figure Income: Battleground Dems Ripped For 'Phony' Working-class Narrative

A 2021 obituary for Gordillo's paternal grandfather, however, raises questions about the family history behind that account, the New York Post reported Saturday.

Manuel Gordillo, Gordillo's grandfather, emigrated from Peru to the United States to practice medicine in 1958. After settling in the United States, Manuel met his future wife in St. Louis, and the couple later had Gordillo's father, Gustavo, per the obituary.

The obituary also notes that Gordillo's grandfather built a successful life as a psychiatrist in Ohio, at one point serving as the president of the Ohio Psychiatric Association, casting doubt on the socialist's claim that his parents grew up in poverty.

"My dad, his first job in the United States was working at Wendy's, my mom's first job was a house cleaner, and they did make a living for themselves, and they had success," Gordillo told Fox News in July.

The elder Gordillo's obituary portrays him as a loving and active father, noting that he raised his "children in Lakewood, Ohio" and that "his most cherished role was as a husband, father, grandfather, and uncle/tio."

"Gustavo and his parents were born in Peru and immigrated to the US," a New York City Democratic Socialists of America spokesperson told Fox News Digital following publication. "Gustavo's father grew up in Peru, not in the United States, and the family had limited contact with Gustavo's grandfather, who is the subject of the Post's recent reporting."

The New York City Democratic Socialists of America later told Fox News Digital that their co-chair's father was a product of Gordillo's first marriage.

The questions surrounding Gordillo's account of his family history come after discrepancies emerged over how he has described his occupation and living arrangements.

Democratic Socialist Headed For $142K Legislature Salary Begs For Rent Handout, Deletes Post After Backlash

The 38-year-old socialist, for example, told the New York Times that he was renting a modest apartment in the Crown Heights neighborhood of Brooklyn only for it to be revealed that he was actually living in a $1.4 million townhouse owned by his father in a trendier part of the borough.

"Not only did DSA co-chair Gustavo Gordillo's parents buy him this rowhouse, they converted it from a two family and renovated it into a luxury single-family home for him," New York City Councilwoman Vickie Paladino said on X. "Exactly the kind of 'greed' the DSA rails against on a daily basis, and reducing valuable housing inventory by one more unit, which is supposedly something the DSA cares very deeply about."

Frustrated Blue-collar Union Bosses Rip Socialist Politicians, Warn Of Labor Exodus From Dem Party

Also undercutting Gordillo's working-class image is his continued self-identification as a "union electrician" despite the fact that he hasn't been a member of the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers since March, when he was fired for not showing up to his apprenticeship.

"After learning of Mr. Gordillo's prolonged absence from and failure to participate in required work and classes, the trustees of the Joint Apprentice Training Committee terminated Mr. Gordillo from the program," the IBEW said in a statement.

Even with the IBEW publicly stating that Gordillo is not a member of their organization, the socialist leader still identifies himself as a "union electrician" on social media.

title: Days after Trump announces Venezuela oil deal, White House fills in some of the details
description: The White House on Monday said it’s partnering with North American Blue Energy Partners as part of President Donald Trump ’s push to tap into Venezuela’s oil industry, setting up a deal that will give...
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The White House on Monday said it's partnering with North American Blue Energy Partners as part of President Donald Trump 's push to tap into Venezuela's oil industry, setting up a deal that will give the Pentagon a stake over roughly a fifth of the country's vast oil reserves.

The Trump administration released more details on Monday night, days after Trump announced what he described as the biggest oil deal in history. The sweeping agreement has been met with skepticism from analysts who say it will take years to revive Venezuela's production, but Trump and his aides are pitching it as a chance to develop a new oil giant in the Western Hemisphere.

As part of the deal, the U.S. is creating a private company as a joint venture with NABEP — a detail the White House had withheld for days. NABEP, owned by Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt, is already the second largest operator in Venezuela, behind Chevron.

Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodríguez is giving the company 100-year rights over 17 oil fields with proven reserves of 65 billion barrels. Many of those fields were previously owned by Russian or Chinese firms, the White House said.

In a statement Monday, Betancourt said Venezuela is "blessed with an abundance of natural resources, hardworking people and untapped potential," adding that the deal will "unleash that potential to the great benefit of both Venezuelans and Americans."

The company said Betancourt had been involved in the Venezuelan oil industry for more than 15 years and said the company has more than 5,000 employees and more than 10,000 contractors.

The deal will give the Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital a 35% ownership stake in the company, the White House disclosed Monday. The U.S. will also be guaranteed a right to purchase 20% of the output at cost, orchestrated through the State Department.

The agreement was signed by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

Betancourt's company has agreed to put up $100 billion in new oil infrastructure investments.

Trump has been pushing to boost oil production in Venezuela since the January military mission that captured then-President Nicolás Maduro on federal narcoterrorism and drug trafficking charges.

The White House claimed the deal would be "at zero cost" to the U.S., and said the government would have veto power on board members — the majority of whom would be U.S. citizens.

"NABEP will have reputable U.S. auditors, lawyers, and advisers and the U.S. government's agreement with NABEP is governed by U.S. law and is subject to the jurisdiction of U.S. courts," the White House said in a fact sheet about the deal.

Former U.S. government energy advisers have cautioned that the deal comes with political risk, since future administrations in Venezuela or the United States could challenge the deal. Even if the agreement holds, analysts say it could take years to turn around Venezuela's dilapidated energy sector.

Trump, who says the plan will reduce gas prices, acknowledged Monday that Americans won't see change right away. Asked about a timeline at the White House, Trump said "it could be a little bit" for prices to fall, and he played down analyst predictions that it could take years.

"If it was two years, you know, that's a short period of time," he said.

Trump said the deal will provide a source to help refill America's strategic oil reserves, which have been drawn down as the Iran war chokes global oil shipments. He added that Venezuela's heavy oil will also go toward producing asphalt and other goods.

"It was this unbelievable value that was sitting dormant," Trump said of Venezuelan oil. "But we're going to be taking all of that."

Rodríguez has also spoken in favor of the deal, describing it as a chance to modernize the Venezuela's oil industry and accelerate its revival. Facing criticism that the deal cedes Venezuelan resources to the U.S., Rodríguez insisted her country's sovereignty remains secure.

Lawmakers on Capitol Hill said Monday that they were looking 

Rep. Rick Crawford, the Republican chairman of the House Intelligence Committee, said he wanted to hear details from the Trump administration "hopefully sooner rather than later."

Sen. Jack Reed, the top Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee, said a deal that uses the military to boost a private oil venture should be rejected and said he wanted a full accounting of the legal authority for the agreement.

"President Trump's effort to turn the U.S. military into an investor in Venezuelan oil is a blatant abuse of power and taxpayer dollars," Reed said in a statement.

The new details were released a day before Trump plans to meet with a group of large and small oil refiners to discuss ways to increase America's capacity to refine oil into gasoline.

The meeting occurs as the Iran war has driven prices at the pump to a national average of $4.08, a 28% increase over the past year, according to AAA.

The White House has said that increasing the number of refineries and expanding the capacity at existing facilities would eventually reduce prices for consumers. The administration also sees the need for more refineries to process oil from Venezuela.

Also attending the meeting will be Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Jarrod Agen, the director of the White House National Energy Dominance Council.

AP Congressional Correspondent Lisa Mascaro contributed to this report.

title: Ms Rachel confronted on accusing Israel of 'genocide' in park interaction with podcaster
description: Podcaster Avi Lichtschein described confronting YouTuber Ms. Rachel at a park, where he asked her about her past comments criticizing Israel for "genocide."
fullText:
Podcaster Avi Lichtschein confronted popular children's educator Ms. Rachel about her anti-Israel comments during an interaction at a neighborhood park, according to the Sunday episode of his show, "Depends on the Context."

During the episode, Lichtschein described running into the YouTuber, whose real name is Rachel Griffin Accurso, while they were both taking their children to the park. After meeting her, he asked her why she was anti-Israel. Accurso reportedly told him that she was not anti-Israel, but anti-Israeli government and anti-Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

"I pushed back on this, and I said, 'That's absurd,'" Lichtschein said. "Saying you're anti-Netanyahu, but you're not anti-Israel? Netanyahu is the democratically elected leader of the sovereign nation. I think what [she does] is way beyond that."

Youtube Star Ms Rachel Gives Funds To Democratic Socialist Michigan Senate Hopeful Abdul El-sayed

Lichtschein said that Accurso also accused Israel of committing a "genocide" through its war with Hamas.

"She said something along the lines of, 'Twenty thousand children have died. How is that not a genocide?'" Lichtschein said. "The answer is — and this is what I was trying to convey to her — genocide is not just a word for, like, a war. War is terrible. Again, Hamas started this war. Genocide is the specific accusation that [she's] hurling at the Jewish people, hurling at the state of Israel, and now it gives carte blanche to go open season on Jews literally around the world."

Lichtschein added that Accurso repeatedly said that her "husband's father is Jewish" and that she supports the existence of a Jewish state. He informed her that she was "spreading blood libel" and that there was "blood on your hands" for her ignorance before she ultimately walked away.

Scholar Challenges Ms Rachel's Gaza Messaging As Antisemitism Surges Globally

Lichtschein then spoke to Accurso's husband on the matter, apologizing for upsetting her, though he did not take back his comments.

"I wasn't planning on changing her mind," Lichstein said. "I wanted to point out your words are creating a lot of damage and someone with an audience as enormous as hers has a responsibility to understand what happens downstream from the things that she says. I think that what she's doing is motivated by compassion for children, but I think she's very naïve and gullible and doesn't realize what her actions are doing to the Jewish community at large, what her words are doing to the enemy of the Jewish people. What she's doing is harmful."

Fox News Digital reached out to Accurso for comment.

Youtube Star Ms Rachel Emotionally Apologizes For Liking Antisemitic Comment, Says It Was An Accident

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Lichtschein recalled that Accurso told him that she considers herself a "Zionist" akin to former New York City Comptroller Brad Lander.

"The timing struck me because it was such a vivid example of the point I had been trying to make to Rachel. You may personally consider yourself a Zionist and may not intend your rhetoric to contribute to hostility toward Jews or Zionists, but when you have an enormous platform, you have to think seriously about what happens downstream from the rhetoric you amplify," Lichtschein said.

He added, "I don't think Rachel hates Jews, and I'm sure her advocacy comes from a place of genuine compassion for children. But when you have an audience as enormous as hers, you have a responsibility to understand the consequences of the claims you're amplifying. That's what I wanted her to hear."
